questions.q: In the SDK's streaming pattern, what does iterating over stream.text_stream give you?
options: The complete raw SSE event objects, including message_start and message_stop
Each text fragment as it arrives, without needing to parse raw SSE events yourself
The token usage counts for the request
A single string containing the entire reply, available only after the stream ends
questions.explain: stream.text_stream is the SDK's higher-level wrapper — it yields each text fragment as it streams in, handling the content_block_delta parsing from Lesson 16 under the hood.

questions.q: Why must the assistant's completed reply be manually appended to the messages list after streaming finishes?
options: It doesn't need to be — the SDK does this automatically
Because assistant replies are never part of the conversation history
Because the SDK's stream() call does not automatically add the completed reply to your messages list for you
Because max_tokens would be exceeded otherwise
questions.explain: The SDK streams text back to you, but it's your responsibility to accumulate the full reply and append it to messages — otherwise the next turn would be missing the model's previous answer.

questions.q: Where does the system prompt go in a streaming client.messages.stream(...) call?
options: As a message in the messages list with role 'system'
It cannot be used together with streaming
Inside the user's first message as plain text
As its own separate system parameter, not inside the messages list
questions.explain: Per Lesson 14, Anthropic's API uses a separate top-level system parameter — it's passed the same way whether or not streaming is used.

questions.q: Why does the messages list need to grow and be resent on every single API call, rather than just sending the latest user message?
options: Because the API rejects requests with fewer than 10 messages
Because streaming requires at least 5 messages to start
Because the model has no memory between calls — the full messages history is how it 'remembers' the conversation (Lesson 4)
It doesn't need to grow — a single message is always sufficient
questions.explain: As established in Chapter 1 (Lesson 4), the model has no memory of its own — resending the growing messages list on every call is what gives the illusion of a remembered conversation.

questions.q: Which of the following is listed as a natural extension of this capstone build that reuses a concept from an earlier chapter?
options: Adding a tools parameter for function/tool calling, from Lesson 17
Rewriting the entire application in a different programming paradigm
Removing the system prompt entirely to simplify the code
Switching away from the Messages API to a completely different protocol
questions.explain: The lesson lists tool calling (Lesson 17), structured JSON output (Lesson 18), and image content blocks (Lesson 26) as extensions that reuse concepts already covered, without changing the loop's basic shape.
